object_description: well-proportioned two-story volume enclosing differentiated outdoor spaces
design_condition: The compact two-story building follows the local grain and surrounding clinic orientation, closes the site toward the residential area, and organizes entrances and outdoor spaces around its eastern traffic routes and southern courtyard.

positive.statement: The well-proportioned volume fits very well into the existing local grain.

position.rationale: Outer volume is clearly visible as a compact, regular two-story perimeter across all calibrated views.

positive.statement: The surrounding open spaces are redefined clearly, with a pleasant green space in front of the building and a courtyard formed by the existing buildings.

position.rationale: Top view identifies the eastern courtyard-like opening and southern foreground as the relevant open-space region.

positive.statement: The entrances are easy to find and readily accessible for operational processes.

position.rationale: Entrances are assigned to the lower eastern edge, consistent with the stated eastern traffic routes.

positive.statement: The building expression provides appropriate livability without the harshness of a prison.

position.rationale: The architectural expression applies to the visible two-story envelope and banded facade treatment.

positive.statement: The clearly structured floor plan implements complex usage processes and security requirements optimally.

position.rationale: The internal plan is not directly resolved, so the marker is constrained to the sampled mid-level region.

positive.statement: Naturally lit corridors and vertically connected outdoor spaces create spaciousness and differentiated movement areas.

position.rationale: Corridors are interior and indistinct; the marker uses the central courtyard-adjacent zone and middle height.

positive.statement: The project fully meets requirements for operation and security through a carefully developed spatial structure.

position.rationale: Operational and security structure is treated as a whole-building judgment on the compact visible envelope.

negative.statement: The entrances are somewhat removed from public view, despite remaining easy to find and accessible.

position.rationale: Public visibility concern is assigned to the lower eastern approach facade mentioned by the design condition.

negative.statement: The playing field is rather tight and its limited clear height may require an exchange of uses between floors.

position.rationale: The playing field is not distinguishable, so it is approximated within the visible open courtyard region.

negative.statement: The building volume and construction costs are on the higher side in comparison.

position.rationale: Volume is directly represented by the compact two-story envelope; cost has no separate geometric location.

negative.statement: Areas, volumes and building standards need revision to optimize costs.

position.rationale: Areas and volumes correspond to the visible building envelope; standards are evaluated globally.

negative.statement: The span of the ground-floor walking yard needs to be revised.

position.rationale: The yard is assigned to the low eastern-southern open-space edge visible in the top and adjacent elevations.

negative.statement: The roof design and solar systems must account for supervision from neighbouring buildings.

position.rationale: Roof systems are anchored at the upper building surface; neighbouring supervision constrains the judgment.

negative.statement: The height of the vehicle-lock gate must be adjusted to the required clearance.

position.rationale: The gate is approximated at the lower eastern vehicle-access edge identified by the site condition.
